description: What a ground reader sees at the next contact: the planned gap, then each log as a catch-up (what happened, what was done, what is being watched, where advice would help), oldest first. Reading it changes nothing aboard. Illustrative only: not seed data.

what_happened: Mara Okafor: heart racing since this morning, comes and goes, easing. No chest pain, fainting or hard breathing.
Pulse at rest 96 bpm by camera, Sim. Rhythm: needs an ECG, not aboard.
what_was_done: 09:39 A crewmate feels your pulse at the wrist for 60 seconds while the cameras count it. Tomas Lind counted 92 in 60 seconds, felt regular; cameras 96; they agree.
being_watched: Measure your pulse at the camera station again, sitting still. Next check: interval to be set by clinical review
If it keeps coming back or happens more often, tell the medical officer.

what_happened: Tomas Lind needs help at the airlock. Eye injury or something in the eye.
Air safe. Tomas Lind responding. No heavy bleeding. Eye injury, chemical or dust in the eye.
what_was_done: 12:03 Chemical, dust or grit in the eye: hold the eye open and rinse with lots of clean water at once, for at least 20 minutes.
12:03 In weightlessness, water and dust float. Use the onboard eye wash set. Until it is ready, rinse with a drink bag and soak up the water with towels.
Crew called at 12:02. Ilya Brandt helping.
advice_welcome: A crewmate repeats the sight check and the photo, and keeps both for the log.
Something stuck in the eye, a chemical in the eye, or any change in sight: call the medical officer at once.
